steps: Read shader.fh with read_file and tell me what it does.
expected: read_file treats shader.fh as text and returns its source lines to the model.
defect: read_file classifies the .fh file as an image and sends it as inline image data; the API answers "The image data you provided does not represent a valid image... (Status: 400)" and the model falls back to cat via the shell.

fault location.explanation: Trusts mime.lookup(), which maps .fh to image/x-freehand, and returns 'image' before any content sniffing; PR #2726 excludes the FreeHand extensions (.fh, .fh4, .fh5, .fh7, .fhc) from this short-circuit.
Same mime-type short-circuit in the core copy of detectFileType; PR #2726 applies the same exclusion.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/2726. read_file decides how to read a file with detectFileType, which in v0.10.0 first asks mime.lookup() for the extension and returns 'image' for any image/* type. mime-db maps the FreeHand family (.fh and variants) to image/x-freehand, so plain-text shader sources with a .fh extension are base64-encoded and sent to the model as an image part, which the provider rejects with a 400 'not a valid image' error. Commit e83eb8f (PR #2726, 'Stop classifying .fh-family files as images') excludes .fh, .fh4, .fh5, .fh7 and .fhc from the mime short-circuit in both the tools and core copies so they fall through to content-based text/binary detection. The fix first ships in v0.11.0, the pinned version, so the case is tested at v0.10.0, the version named in the issue.

_meta.notes: Issue page: CLOSED/COMPLETED, closing PR #2726 MERGED; main commit e83eb8f (first tag v0.11.0, ancestor of pinned); ac86036 is the PR head. PR #3075 (also linked) only changes the retry advice after a 400 and is not the fix. The fix applies cleanly to v0.10.0 (no diff between v0.10.0 and the fix parent in these files). Reported on Windows with gpt-5.6-sol; the misclassification is platform independent, but whether the shared ABB endpoint returns a 400 for the bogus image part is uncertain; the outgoing image part is observable in model traffic.
